Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:3.hebrew: אבל אם אמר הרי הנטיעות האלו קרבן עדי שיקצצו אין להם פדיון - לעולם, כל זמן שלא נקצצו, ואין יוצאין לחולין, אלא קדושות הן, שהן בקדושת הגוף לעולם, ואין להם תקנה עולמית, שאפילו פדאן, חוזרות וקדושות. דכיון דאמר עד שיקצצו, אין להם פדיון לעולם כל זמן שלא נקצצו, משמע דלעולם יהיו קרבן עד שיקצצו:
Rashi on Nedarim 28a:14:3.english: But if he said, "These saplings are [hereby] an offering until they are cut down," they have no redemption - [That is, they have no redemption] ever, as long as they have not been cut down, and they do not go out to non-sacred status; rather, they remain consecrated, for they possess inherent sanctity forever, and they have no permanent remedy, for even if one redeemed them, they revert to being consecrated. For since he said, "until they are cut down," they have no redemption ever as long as they have not been cut down — [his statement] implies that they shall forever be an offering until they are cut down.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:2:1.hebrew: וליתני - בהאי לישנא ברישא, דהיכא דאמר "הרי הפירות האלו קרבן [אם אינם נקצצות]", "קדושות ואינן קדושות". קדושות — דחל קדושה עלייהו, ואינן קדושות — דיש להן פדיון, דלפי ההוא עניין דקתני סיפא הויין "קדושות ואינן קדושות". דאילו בסיפא דהתם, דאמר "עד שיקצצו", הוי קדושה גמורה, שהרי הן בקדושת הגוף שאין להם פדיון כל זמן שאין נקצצות, אע"ג דקדושת דמים הוא; ואילו כי אמר "אם אינן נקצצות", ליכא קדושה חמורה, שהרי יש להם פדיון. ולהכי, כי אמר "אם אינן נקצצות", לענין כי אמר "עד שיקצצו" "קדושות ואינן קדושות" הן:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:2:1.english: And let [the Mishnah] teach - using this phrasing in the first clause: that where one says, "These fruits are [like] a sacrifice [if they are not cut down]," [let it teach] "they are consecrated and not consecrated." "Consecrated," in that sanctity takes effect upon them; and "not consecrated," in that they are subject to redemption — for relative to that case which the latter clause teaches, they are "consecrated and not consecrated." For whereas in the latter clause there, where one says "until they are cut down," it is a complete sanctity, since they are [treated as having] inherent sanctity in that they have no redemption as long as they are not cut down, even though it is [only] monetary sanctity; whereas when one says "if they are not cut down," there is no stringent sanctity, since they are subject to redemption. Therefore, when one says "if they are not cut down," relative to when one says "until they are cut down," they are "consecrated and not consecrated."

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:2:2.hebrew: תריץ, אין הכי נמי הוה ליה למתני, אלא איידי וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:2:2.english: [The Gemara] answers: Indeed, it should have taught [so]; rather, since [it wanted to teach the latter clause,] etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:3:1.hebrew: א"כ למה ליה למימר - דחל קדושה עלייהו, כיון שעבר היום ולא נקצצו:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:3:1.english: If so, why does he need to say [it] - That sanctity takes effect upon them, since the day passed and they were not cut down.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:3:2.hebrew: לא צריכא כגון דאיכא זיקא נפישא - שמנשבת רוח קשה בעולם, דמסיק אדעתיה דמיתבר להו זיקא, דהיינו נקצצות. וסד"א לא גמר בלבו להקדישו, אלא אדעתא דמיתבר להו זיקא אמר הכי, ולא צריכי פדיון, דלא חל עלייהו קדושה וכחולין דמי. קמ"ל דחל קדושה עלייהו, דלהקדש גמור מתכוין:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:3:2.english: It is only necessary where there is a strong wind - For a fierce wind is blowing in the world, so he assumes that the wind will break them, which is [tantamount to being] "cut down." And you might have thought [to say that] he did not resolve in his heart to consecrate it, rather he spoke thus on the assumption that the wind would break them, and [therefore] they do not require redemption, because sanctity did not take effect upon them and they are like non-sacred [produce]. [Therefore, it] teaches us that sanctity does take effect upon them, for he intended a complete consecration.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:1.hebrew: [והא וכו'] - כלומר, היכי מצית אמרת דאיכא זיקא נפישא, והקתני לה דומיא דטלית, וטלית מי קיימא לשרפה? בתמיה:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:1.english: [But isn't, etc.] - That is to say, how can you say that there is a strong wind, when it teaches it similarly to [the case of] a garment — and is a garment ready for burning? [This is] a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:2.hebrew: אין כגון דאיכא דליקה - ומסיק אדעתיה דלא מיתצל, ולהכי קאמר "אם אינה נשרפת":
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:2.english: Yes, in a case where there is a fire - And he thinks to himself that [it] will not be saved, and therefore he says, "if it is not burned."

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:3.hebrew: הכי נמי וכו' - וסד"א דלא מתכוין להקדש כלל, כדפרשינן:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:3.english: So too, etc. - And you might have thought that he does not intend [it] for consecration at all, as we explained.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:4.hebrew: קמ"ל - דחל קדושה עלייהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:4:4.english: [It] teaches us - that sanctity takes effect upon them.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:5:1.hebrew: ולעולם - בתמיה. מדקתני אין להן פדיון, משמע שלעולם אין להם פדיון אפי' לאחר קציצה:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:5:1.english: And forever - [This is asked] in astonishment. Since [the Mishnah] teaches "they have no redemption," it implies that they never have redemption, even after [they are] cut down.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:5:2.hebrew: אמר בר פדא - כל זמן שלא נקצצו, עדיין חוזרות וקדושות:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:5:2.english: Bar Padda said - As long as they have not been cut down, they still become consecrated again.

Rashi on Nedarim 28b:5:3.hebrew: נקצצו פודן פעם אחת ודיו - ויצאו לחולין, ושוב אינו פודן, דהא חולין הן:
Rashi on Nedarim 28b:5:3.english: [Once] they are cut down, he redeems them once and it is sufficient - And they go out to non-sacred [status], and he does not redeem them again, for they are non-sacred.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:2:1.hebrew: <big><abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> </big>רבינו שמואל: "וליתני קדושות", <abbr title="ולא גרסינן">ול"ג</abbr> "ואין קדושות" — דמשמע דפריך וליתני בסיפא דאינה קדושה, ואדרבה בסיפא קדושה טפי, דאין להם פדיון היינו דאין מועיל להן פדיון, כדקאמר בסמוך; אלא גרסינן "וליתני קדושות" ותו לא, וארישא פריך. <abbr title="ורבינו יצחק">ור"י</abbr> [פירש] דשפיר גרסינן ליה, ותרווייהו קיימי ארישא, ופריך הכי: וליתני "הרי אלו קדושות אם אינם נקצצות, ואינם קדושות אם נקצצו", וממילא ידעינן דפשיטא דיש להן פדיון כשאר כל חרמי דמים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:2:1.english: Rabbeinu Shmuel reads [the Gemara] as follows: "And let [the Mishnah] teach: 'they are consecrated,'" and he does not read "and they are not consecrated" — because [that] implies that [the Gemara] is asking that it should teach in the latter clause that it is not consecrated, whereas on the contrary, in the latter clause it is consecrated even more, for "they have no redemption" means that redemption is ineffective for them, as [the Gemara] says immediately below; rather, we read "And let it teach: 'they are consecrated'" and nothing more, and [the Gemara] is asking on the first clause. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak [explained] that we properly read it [the full phrase], and both [parts] refer to the first clause, and [the Gemara] is asking as follows: Let [the Mishnah] teach, "Behold, these are consecrated if they are not cut down, and they are not consecrated if they were cut down," and automatically we would know that it is obvious that they have redemption like all other consecrations of monetary value.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:2:2.hebrew: איידי דבעי למיתני בסיפא אין להם פדיון - כלומר, שאין פדיון מועיל בהם, דלעולם חוזרות וקדושו' כדמסיק — תנא נמי רישא יש להם פדיון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:2:2.english: Since it wanted to teach in the latter clause, "They have no redemption" - That is to say, redemption is not effective for them, for they always revert and become consecrated [again], as [the Gemara] concludes — it also taught [in] the first clause, "They have redemption."

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:3:1.hebrew: היכי נדר - פר"י דאי סתם כדקתני ולא נתן זמן לקציצתן, א"כ אינם קצוצות, ואין לך קצוצות דאינם נקצצות לסוף אלף שנים מחמת שהיא מתייבשת:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:3:1.english: How did he take a vow? - Ri explained that if [he vowed] without specifying, as [the Mishnah] teaches, and did not set a time for their cutting, if so, they are not cut down, and you have none that are cut down, for they are not cut down at the end of a thousand years because it dries out.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:3:2.hebrew: דאיכא זיקא נפישא - וא"ת: מה ענין זה לשאר נדרים דלעיל, דקתני ד' נדרים התירו? וי"ל: משום דמהו דתימא דחשיב נדרי זרוזין, שאין נדר אלא לאמן דבריו שלא יתנצלו, ולא משום דדעתו להקדישם אם ינצלו — קמ"ל דאפ"ה הוו קדושות, דגמר בלבו להקדישם, [שסבור] הוא שיכול להיות דמינצלן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:3:2.english: Where there is a great wind - And if you ask: What connection does this have to the other vows above, where [the Mishnah] teaches: "[The Sages] permitted four vows"? And one can answer: [This case is needed] because what might you have said? That it is considered [one of the] vows of motivation (nidrei zeruzin), for he only vowed to reinforce his words that they would not be spared, and not because his intention was to consecrate them if they are spared — [therefore, the Gemara] teaches us that even so they become consecrated, because he resolved in his heart to consecrate them, [for] he [thinks] that it is possible that they will be spared.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:5:1.hebrew: אין להם פדיון ולעולם - בתמיה: וכי לעולם לא יהא להם פדיון? דפשיטא ליה ד"אין להם פדיון" ר"ל שאין מועיל להם פדיון, כמקדש וככלים דאין להם פדיון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:5:1.english: "They have no redemption." "And forever?" - [This is asked] in astonishment: can it be that forever they will have no redemption? For it is obvious to [the Gemara] that "they have no redemption" means that redemption is not effective for them, like the Temple and [its] vessels, which have no redemption.

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:5:2.hebrew: אמר בר פדא פדאן חוזרות וקדושות וכן לעולם עד שיקצצו - שכך ר"ל: "הרי הן קרבן עד שיקצצו", דכל שאפדם — תחזור ותחול קדושה עליהם כל שעה. נקצצו — פודן פעם אחת, דקדושה שבהן לא פקעה בכדי, אע"ג ד"עד שיקצצו" קאמר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:5:2.english: Bar Padda said: [If] he redeemed them, they become consecrated again, and so [on] forever until they are cut down - For this is what [the vower] means to say: "They are an offering until they are cut down" — that whenever I redeem them, consecration shall return and take effect upon them at all times. [Once] they are cut down, he redeems them once, for the consecration within them does not expire on its own, even though he said, "until they are cut down."

Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:5:3.hebrew: עולא אמר כיון שנקצצו שוב אין פודן - דלא הקדישן אלא עד שיקצצו, דפקעה קדושה בכדי כשנקצצו. וצ"ע לעולא אם [פדאן] חוזרות וקדושות או לא. וי"ל שמודה דאם פדאן חוזרות וקדושות כל זמן שלא נקצצו, כמו לבר פדא; דמדלא פליג עליה — שהרי שיטה דהש"ס משמע כן, מדפריך "ולעולם?", משמע פשיטא ליה ד"אין להם פדיון" דקאמר, היינו דאינן בתורת פדיון, דפשיטא ליה דעד שיקצצו הם קדושות. וא"ת: מנלן דלעולא חוזרות וקדושות? וכ"ת מל' "עד שיקצצו" — הא איצטריך לעולא לכוין לשון כשנקצצו דשוב אין פודן, כדפרישית, וא"כ מנ"ל דפדאן חוזרות וקדושות קודם קציצה? וי"ל דא"כ הוה ליה למימר (לנודר): "הרי הנטיעות האלו קרבן עד שנקצצו ולא יותר", או אומר "אינם קרבן אלא עד שנקצצו", ואז משמע תרתי: משמע דפדאן חוזרות וקדושות קודם קציצה, ומשמע נמי דאחר קדושה פקעה קדושה מנייהו, מדלא אמר "הרי הן כקרבן לעולם":
Tosafot on Nedarim 28b:5:3.english: Ulla said: Once they are cut down, one does not redeem them again - because he consecrated them only until they are cut down, so the sanctity expires on its own when they are cut down. And it requires further study according to Ulla whether, if [he redeemed them], they revert and become consecrated or not. And one can say that he agrees that if he redeemed them, they revert and become consecrated as long as they have not been cut down, just as according to Bar Padda; for since he does not dispute him [on this] — for indeed the flow of the Talmud implies this, since it asks, "And forever?", it implies that it is obvious to [the Gemara] that [when the Mishnah] states "they have no redemption," it means that they are not subject to [permanent] redemption, since it is obvious to [the Gemara] that until they are cut down they are consecrated. And if you ask: From where do we know that according to Ulla they revert and become consecrated? And if you say [it is derived] from the wording "until they are cut down" — [that cannot be, because] that is needed for Ulla to convey the wording that when they are cut down one does not redeem them again, as I explained; and if so, from where does he know that if he redeemed them they revert and become consecrated before cutting? And one can say that if so [i.e., if it meant only that sanctity expires upon cutting], he (the vower) should have said: "These saplings are an offering until they are cut down and no more," or said: "They are not an offering except until they are cut down," and then it would imply both things: it implies that if he redeemed them, they revert and become consecrated before cutting, and it also implies that after [they are cut down (lit. after consecration)] the sanctity departs from them, since he did not say, "Behold, they are like an offering forever."
